reviews.pullQuote: I would ship A2UI: one catalog, native widgets on web, SwiftUI, Compose, and Flutter, for people and agents.
reviews.testimonial: I would choose A2UI when the same interface has to be used by a person and generated by an agent on more than one platform. The catalog is the contract: the agent may only emit component types and functions the client has registered, and createSurface plus updateComponents stream a flat adjacency list that the React, SwiftUI, Flutter, and Jetpack Compose renderers turn into native widgets rather than a WebView. People get the host's accessibility APIs and theme; agents get schema validation and action events back, including v1.0's callRendererFunction. Against json-render, I give up a ready-made 36-component shadcn catalog and renderers for email, PDF, and Slack cards. I would rather close A2UI's Compose v0.9.1 lag than split the wire format per framework.
reviews.evaluations:
**A2UI** — This is the toolkit I would build on. A catalog is a JSON Schema contract of components, functions, and prompt instructions; the agent streams a flat adjacency list with createSurface and updateComponents, and each renderer maps those types to native widgets. Official SDKs cover React, Lit, and Angular, Flutter and SwiftUI on v0.9.1 and v1.0, and Jetpack Compose with material3-a2ui on v0.9.1 only. v1.0 dropped hardcoded theme colors so the host theme wins, maps accessibility onto host APIs, and adds callRendererFunction and callAgentFunction so behavior stays in the catalog instead of executable UI code. The observed gap is version skew: Compose is published at v0.9.1 on the SDK page while the current spec is v1.0, so a multi-platform session has to negotiate. Arbitrary canvases are outside the basic catalog; the documented escape is embedding an MCP App in a surface, not pretending the catalog is a browser. [SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/), [catalogs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/catalogs/), [v1.0 spec](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/).

**json-render** — The closest generative-UI alternative. defineCatalog plus Zod guardrails the model; SpecStream paints partial specs; @json-render/shadcn ships 36 components, and there are renderers for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, React Native, Ink, PDF, email, chat cards, and @json-render/mcp. The README's "same catalog" line does not match the install samples: web and React Native import different schema modules, and there is no SwiftUI or Compose renderer. I would use it for a web-plus-Expo product whose extra surfaces are email and Slack. A single negotiated schema with native Apple and Android renderers would answer that objection. [README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render).

**MCP Apps** — The right protocol when a tool needs a chart, form, or canvas inline in Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Goose, or Postman. A tool declares a ui:// HTML resource, the host renders a sandboxed iframe, and the view talks back over PostMessageTransport and can call other tools. That is a host extension, not a design system, and the UI is HTML rather than SwiftUI or Compose. Host support varies. I would embed MCP Apps inside an A2UI surface for the interactions a catalog cannot express, which is the relationship both projects already document, rather than make iframes the product UI on every platform. [README](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps).

**Ouro UI** — The best human-craft system in the set, and the only one that splits the brief on purpose. Ouro HX is copy-in React on Base UI and Tailwind v4, with ouro-check walking built pages from 320 to 3840 in light and dark for overlap, clipped text, and axe-core violations. Ouro AX is a separate kit for CLIs, HTTP, and MCP: one command definition becomes a parser, JSON help, and an MCP tool, and ax-xray checks claims from outside. The Apple package (0.2.1) shares tokens and an App Intents X-ray, but the Apple page says components are still in the workshop, and Feel and Reins are not in that release. There is no Android half and no shared surface an agent composes for a person. If the job were "agents operate Apple apps while people feel the springs," I would start here. It does not render one agent-authored UI across web and native. [llms.txt](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/llms.txt), [Apple](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/apple/).

**Agent-native (Builder.io)** — defineAction is the right shared capability layer: one Zod schema and one run(), mounted as a React hook, an agent tool, HTTP, MCP, A2A, and a CLI, with the same validation, permissions, and audit trail. The documented client is a React app; the agent does not render or click the UI, it calls the action layer. I would put those actions behind an A2UI catalog's functions, not use Agent-Native as the interface toolkit. A native skin on the same actions would still not give agents a layout language. [Actions overview](https://www.agent-native.com/docs/actions-overview/).

**CopilotKit** — The runtime I would use to put an agent in front of users, not the design contract. CopilotRuntime streams over AG-UI into React, Angular, Vue, React Native, Slack, and Teams, with shared state, human-in-the-loop, frontend tools, and generative UI that can include A2UI and sandboxed MCP Apps. Passing a2ui: {} renders A2UI inside chat. The docs page still calls A2UI a JSONL spec, which does not match the v1.0 envelopes on a2ui.org, so I would not let that chat renderer be the source of truth for SwiftUI or Compose clients. [A2UI in CopilotKit](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/generative-ui/a2ui).

**Vercel UI SDK** — The behavior layer I would want coding agents to assemble on the web. definePrimitive and slots live in @ui-sdk/core; createParts renders them in React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components; a ui-sdk skill and a WebMCP path let a browser agent read and call components. The llms.txt lists those five web targets and no native adapter, and the project is in beta with APIs that may still change. It solves "agents build the component," not "agents and people share a running native UI." A SwiftUI or Compose adapter of the same behaviors is not in the docs I read. [llms.txt](https://ui-sdk.dev/llms.txt).

**OpenAI Apps SDK UI** — A Tailwind 4 token set and Radix-based React components, including Badge, Button, and AppsSDKUIProvider, tuned for ChatGPT apps on React 18 or 19. It is a host skin, not a catalog protocol and not a native renderer. MCP Apps ships a migrate-oai-app skill, which is the right reading of where this sits: inside an Apps SDK or MCP iframe, under a cross-platform contract rather than as the contract. [README](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui).

**AI Elements** — Conversation, message, and code-block components on shadcn/ui and the AI SDK, copied into the app as source. The README warns the project will be deprecated at the end of November 2026 in favor of shadcn/ui's AI Elements. It is Next.js chat chrome, not a general interface catalog, and it has no native target. I would not start a dual-audience system on a library scheduled to disappear within weeks of this cutoff. [README](https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements).

**shadcn/ui** — Copy-in, open-code components you own, distributed as a registry and now founded on Base UI. That is the right distribution model for a web catalog — Ouro and json-render both use it — and a good visual layer for an A2UI React renderer. It is not a protocol, has no native targets, and does not give an agent a validated surface to drive. Owning the source answers customization; it does not answer cross-platform agent use. [README](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui).

**Base UI** — Unstyled accessible React primitives from the Radix, Floating UI, and Material UI authors. The quick start I fetched is v1.9.0, with portal stacking, composition, and an llms.txt so an authoring agent can read the docs. Ouro and shadcn sit on it. It is web React only. An llms.txt helps an agent write the component; it does not let an agent use the running interface on iOS or Android. [Quick start](https://base-ui.com/react/overview/quick-start).

**Radix UI** — Low-level unstyled accessible primitives, MIT-licensed, still documented at radix-ui.com/primitives. No agent protocol and no native renderer. I would not start a new system here when Base UI, from the same authors, is what shadcn's --base base and Ouro both target. That is an overlap judgment from those projects' docs, not a deprecation notice I found in the Radix README itself. [README](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives).

**MUI** — A decade of battle-tested React components implementing Material Design, extended by MUI X for complex widgets. The README still points the design system at m2.material.io. It is React web only: no catalog, no action stream back to an agent, no SwiftUI path. I would reuse its component knowledge inside a custom A2UI web catalog, and use material3-a2ui on Android, rather than make MUI the cross-platform contract. [README](https://github.com/mui/material-ui).

**Chakra UI** — Accessible React components with RSC support, styled through Emotion, plus a Cursor MCP install deeplink so a coding agent can read the library. That MCP server is for the docs, not for the product UI. There is no native renderer and no generative catalog. Composition speed for human developers does not get an agent onto iOS. [README](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui).

**Fluent UI** — Microsoft's web collection: @fluentui/react-components v9 with Griffel, slots, and accessible-by-default components used by Microsoft 365, plus v8 and web components used by Edge. This repository is web. I did not find an agent UI protocol in the README, and Fluent's native siblings are other repos, not this candidate. Strong if the product is M365 on the web; the wrong contract for an agent composing phone UI. [README](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui).

**React Aria and React Spectrum** — The accessibility bar I would steal from, not the system I would adopt. React Aria implements WAI-ARIA authoring practices with mouse, touch, and keyboard, and ships internationalization for 30+ languages; the README says React Stately can also be used on other platforms such as React Native. React Spectrum is Adobe's styled web system. There is no agent catalog and no SwiftUI or Compose mapping. I would copy its interaction and i18n lessons into an A2UI catalog's checks and accessibility envelope. [README](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum).

**Tamagui** — The serious way to share human UI between web and React Native: an optimizing compiler flattens styled trees to a div plus atomic CSS, or a View with hoisted style objects, so you are not paying a WebView tax. There is no agent-facing schema and no SwiftUI or Compose output. If I were not generating UI and only sharing hand-built screens across RN and web, Tamagui beats adding a Flutter shell. It does not let an agent compose the interface. [README](https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui).

**Flutter** — The best single codebase for pixels on iOS, Android, web, and desktop: Material and Cupertino widgets, Impeller, and stateful hot reload, compiling to ARM, JavaScript, and WebAssembly. Agents do not get a catalog unless you add a2ui_flutter, which is why I choose A2UI's Flutter renderer rather than Flutter alone. A Flutter-only app also cannot drop the same surface into an existing SwiftUI or Compose host. [README](https://github.com/flutter/flutter).

**SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines** — The right human system on Apple platforms. SwiftUI declares views, scenes, and an App across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS, and can bridge to UIKit, AppKit, and WatchKit. The HIG covers accessibility, layout, color, typography, and platform adaptation, including Liquid Glass samples. Nothing I fetched is an agent wire protocol. I would implement an A2UI catalog as SwiftUI views so the HIG still governs the pixels, which is what A2UISwiftUI already does. [SwiftUI](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui), [HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines).

**Material 3 and Jetpack Compose** — The right human system on Android. MaterialTheme carries color roles, dynamic color from the wallpaper on Android 12 and above, a type scale, a shape scale, tonal elevation, and a large component set. This page is Android's design system, not a web or iOS renderer, and it has no agent catalog. A2UI's material3-a2ui package is the bridge, and it is the renderer still published at v0.9.1. I would theme the Android catalog with MaterialTheme rather than invent a parallel Material. [Material 3 in Compose](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3).
candidateOrder: SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines
